LanguageData.OCity_AboutGeneralText:
Greetings, Colonist!
OnlineCity is a multiplayer mod for RimWorld that allows multiple players to play on the same planet online.
Each player develops their own colony, sees colonies and caravans of other players, and can interact with them: transfer resources and colonists, trigger events, or attack.
1. Installation and starting the game 2. Basics of multiplayer 3. Transferring property and colonists 4. Events and other interactions 5. PvP — attacking colonies 6. Mods and compatibility 7. Known issues and troubleshooting 8. FAQ 9. Installation and starting the game
Installation 1. Install RimWorld 1.1–1.4. 2. Install Harmony and HugsLib. 3. Install OnlineCity. 4. In the "Mods" menu, order mods roughly like this: Harmony -> Core -> HugsLib -> other mods -> OnlineCity
OnlineCity is recommended to be kept last. Restart the game after changing mod order.
ModsConfig.xml The mod list must start with: brrainz.harmony ludeon.rimworld unlimitedhugs.hugslib
OnlineCity is recommended to be placed at the end: todako.onlinecity
Starting the game 1. In the main menu, select "Multiplayer". 2. Register an account or log into an existing one. 3. Choose a landing site. 4. Create or select colonists. 5. Start the game.
Initial login may take several minutes, especially if the server uses a large modpack.
Before connecting for the first time, it is recommended to make a backup of your Mods and Config folders.
Game saves Multiplayer progress is saved on the server. * Autosave runs every 15 minutes. The interval can be changed in settings. * Saving is also performed when exiting via the game menu. * If you close the game via Alt+F4 or force-quit, unsaved progress will be lost.
For offline play, you can load onlineCityTempLoad, but changes made in it cannot be transferred back to the server.
OnlineCity functions only when launched via the "Multiplayer" menu option.
2. Basics of multiplayer OnlineCity does not alter RimWorld gameplay. Factions, NPCs, events, and other mechanics operate independently for each player. Every player has their own game session and colony, but all players share the same global map.
Colonies and caravans Colonies and caravans of other players are displayed on the world map.
Colonies: * icon appearance roughly indicates its wealth; * light in the colony window shows the player is online; * selecting a colony allows you to view the player, their status, and total colony wealth.
Caravans of other players are also visible on the global map. Caravans display available carrying capacity.
Online chat The "Online" button opens chat and other network features.
In chat, you can: * view the list of all players and online players; * create custom channels; * add other players to channels; * view player information.
3. Transferring property and colonists Transfers between players are carried out exclusively via caravan.
How to transfer property 1. Select your caravan. 2. Right-click on another player's colony or caravan. 3. Select "Trade goods". 4. Specify goods, animals, or colonists to transfer.
You can transfer any amount of property an unlimited number of times. The recipient may be offline.
There is no direct barter window: players negotiate in chat and transfer items sequentially.
Receiving a transfer Upon receiving a transfer, a notification appears listing the transferred property with the option to accept or reject.
If rejected, the transferred property is destroyed.
Accepted items are placed: 1. in the largest stockpile with "торг" or "trad" in its name; 2. if no such stockpile exists, in the largest available stockpile.
Special cases Prisoners. Transferred prisoners appear as passive hostile colonists. You must capture them manually and escort them to prison.
Last caravan colonist. If you transfer the last colonist, the caravan dissolves and all its goods are automatically added to the transfer. To prevent this, leave at least one animal in the caravan.
Colonist relationships. After transferring a colonist, their relationships with other colonists are lost.
Assisting another player The transfer mechanic can be used not only for trading, but also for assistance during raids or other events. For example, you can transfer colonists to an ally and have them sent back after combat ends.
4. Events and other interactions On the global map, you can select another player's colony and trigger various events via the "Interact" menu. For gold, you can summon: pirate raids, tribal raids, insect infestations, mechanoids, toxic fallout, and other events.
Event strength For certain events, you can configure an impact multiplier relative to standard incident strength. The typical maximum multiplier is x10.
Cost depends on colony wealth and event strength: (colony_wealth / 100 000)^(2/3) x 100 x impact_strength^(3/2)
Threat type multipliers * x2 — Industrial tech pirates * x3 — Insects * x5 — Mechanoids
Arrival method multipliers * x1.0 — On foot from map edge * x1.4 — Center drop * x1.5 — Scattered drop
The cost of drop pods is automatically factored into the total raid cost.
Formulas and coefficients may change during balancing. Servers may also set custom cost multipliers and maximum event strengths.
Summoning a raid A summoned raid does not necessarily arrive immediately, and only triggers if the target player is online. If raid strength exceeds 50% of the maximum allowed, a warning is sent half an in-game day in advance.
After a raid, subsequent events cannot trigger sooner than 1 in-game day later. Delay is calculated as: 1 + impact_strength x 0.16666 + 0.03333 x (colony_wealth / 100 000)
Novice protection Combat interaction is only allowed between players meeting both conditions: * both attacker and target have over 2 years of in-game time; * their colony wealth exceeds 100,000.
Event queue Events from different tabs can be queued simultaneously. * One player can add up to 1 event per tab against a target player. * Other players can also queue events against the same target. * Events are executed sequentially, respecting cooldown intervals. * Maximum queue length is 2 events.
5. PvP — attacking colonies PvP allows attacking another player's colony with your caravan. For an attack to proceed, both players must have "Participate in PvP" enabled. You can only attack a player who is online.
Starting the attack Once combat begins, the attacker's caravan spawns at a random map edge.
The attacker can: * scout the colony and retreat; * plunder it; * capture the colony by downing all enemy colonists.
Interior rooms are hidden until doors or walls are breached.
PvP peculiarities Attacker colonist control is handled remotely. Because of this: * movement and commands may experience input delay; * aiming and firing progress are not displayed in real time; * after 1 minute of combat, defender colonists have their movement speed halved to partially compensate for network latency.
During PvP: * game speed is locked to x0.5; * pause and fast-forward are disabled; * time of day and weather match the defender's game.
Colonist commands During an assault, only basic combat orders are available: * movement; * ranged attack; * melee attack; * picking up and dropping items; * switching weapons and apparel; * consuming food and drinks.
Building, deconstructing, using artifacts, and most civilian tasks are unavailable.
Autotargeting is always active.
Once a colony is captured, these restrictions are lifted.
Maximum attacker caravan wealth Attacker caravan wealth cannot exceed: 4 / (25/1 000 000 + 10/colony_wealth)
Examples: Colony wealth: 100,000 | Max caravan wealth: 32,000 Colony wealth: 400,000 | Max caravan wealth: 80,000 Colony wealth: 1,000,000 | Max caravan wealth: 114,400 Colony wealth: 2,000,000 | Max caravan wealth: 133,332
If a caravan is too expensive, divide it or reduce the number of attackers.
Disconnection and retreat If either player disconnects during combat, it is counted as a defeat: * attacker loses their caravan; * defender loses their colony.
Upon disconnect, enemy colonists continue fighting under AI control.
To retreat, use "Withdraw". All colonists within 10 tiles of the map edge will return to the caravan.
Tamable animals in the attacking caravan do not participate in combat. They wait near the map edge until combat ends or retreat is called.
Limitations and known issues * Movement orders may occasionally cancel, causing colonists to start retreating. * Health, inventory, and needs update with latency. * Downed colonists are not auto-targeted and cannot be melee attacked. Use ranged weapons to finish them. * Tiles right at the map boundary are inaccessible to attacker pawns. * Items dropped directly on the map edge can only be collected after the colony is captured. * If a colonist gets stuck near the map edge, select them and right-click different spots further inland until they resume moving.
Servers can configure PvP parameters, including maximum caravan wealth and truce duration between attacks. The default cooldown is 20 minutes.
6. Mods and compatibility OnlineCity can run alongside other mods, but compatibility depends on their mechanics and configuration.
Mod synchronization The server may enforce mod synchronization. In that case, upon logging in, the following may be overwritten: * Mods folder; * ModsConfig.xml file.
Before connecting for the first time, make a backup of your Mods and Config directories.
DLCs are not synchronized. * If the server uses a DLC, you must install and own it yourself. * If the server does not use a DLC, it will be disabled.
If mod sync is turned off, player modlists may differ. The OnlineCity mod version, however, must match the server version.
Items from other mods Take caution when trading modded items. If both players have the mod installed, issues rarely occur.
If the recipient lacks the mod, the item may: * lose properties; * disappear; * cause errors or, in rare cases, corrupt the save.
In case of critical errors, contact server administration to see if save restoration is possible.
World-altering mods It is not recommended to use unsynchronized mods that modify: * terrain generation; * oceans and seas; * mountains; * other world map elements.
If planet generation differs between players, a base might spawn in deep water or become completely inaccessible.
Such mods should only be used if all players have identical modlists and configurations.
Known compatibility issues Currently known incompatible mod: Save Our Ship 2
Other mods can potentially work with OnlineCity, but large modpacks and mods that rewrite core RimWorld mechanics can cause conflicts.
Zetrith Multiplayer can run alongside OnlineCity, as they utilize different networking paradigms: * OnlineCity — one planet with separate colonies; * Zetrith Multiplayer — shared control of a single colony.
7. Known issues and troubleshooting Long loading after login After logging in, OnlineCity may download mods and saves from the server. During this time, the game may: * freeze; * show a black screen; * remain unresponsive for several minutes.
This is not necessarily an error. Usually waiting 5–10 minutes is enough. Initial connection to a server with a large modpack over a slow network can take much longer.
"Not all files passed validation" If this message appears upon connecting, try reconnecting again. It can occur due to minor desyncs in the Mods folder or ModsConfig.xml.
Restart after opening the "Mods" menu If the server uses mod synchronization, opening the "Mods" menu may cause RimWorld to alter ModsConfig.xml. OnlineCity might restart the game on your next login to restore server order. This is expected behavior. When mod sync is enabled, avoid altering your mod list unnecessarily.
Version mismatch Open: "Multiplayer" -> "Guide / FAQ" The OnlineCity version is displayed in the first line and must match the server version.
Username already taken Ensure your login and password are at least 3 Latin characters long, or pick another username if the account is already taken.
Connection issues Unstable internet connections can cause: * sync errors; * download failures; * disconnections.
Mod issues Try temporarily disabling other mods to verify. If the issue disappears, it is likely a mod conflict. Mods that modify PvP logic can break gameplay.
Colonist transfer issue A known issue occurs when transferring colonists with HardcoreSK. Similar conflicts may arise with other overhaul mods.
Duplicate of transferred colonist Occasionally after transferring a colonist, an exact duplicate with identical name, backstory, and skills might appear in another event or ask to join. Do not accept them—witnesses report this is a phantom that crashes the game!
Corrupted save If a colony fails to load or game-breaking errors prevent play, contact the server administrator. When possible, administrators can restore your colony from a previous backup. You can also start a new colony under the same account.
System requirements OnlineCity increases RAM usage. A 64-bit operating system is recommended.
8. FAQ Can we manage a single colony together? No. In normal gameplay, each player controls their own colony. The only exception is attacking another player's settlement, but that is not collaborative colony management. For co-op colony management, consider Zetrith Multiplayer.
What happens to other players when I pause the game? Nothing. Each participant's game runs independently. Pausing only stops your local game. Meanwhile, you can still observe other players' colonies and caravan movements on the world map.
How to select difficulty and AI storyteller? They cannot be changed by players. They are configured by the server administrator during world creation.
How to delete my colony? Open the "Online" window from the bottom menu bar or game menu. In the "About mod" tab, click "Start over". Alternatively, type this command in chat: /killmyallplease
How often does the game save? Typically every 15 minutes. It also saves when exiting through the game menu.
Alt+F4 does NOT trigger an exit save, so the colony will roll back to the last autosave.
What if I forget my password? An administrator can reset your password using the command: /ChangePassword {UserLogin} {NewPassword}
Administrators are advised to verify account ownership before resetting passwords.
Is developer mode available? This depends on server settings. If developer mode is disabled by the server, players cannot enable it.
Where are OnlineCity logs located? Logs are saved at: %appdata%\..\LocalLow\Ludeon Studios\RimWorld by Ludeon Studios\OnlineCity
This path can be pasted directly into Windows Explorer address bar.
